name: Walter Molino
description: Walter Molino (1915–1997) was a prominent Italian illustrator and comic artist, widely regarded as one of the 20th century's masters of visual storytelling. He is most famous for his long-standing collaboration with the weekly magazine La Domenica del Corriere , where he created iconic cover illustrations that captured dramatic news events, historical moments, and scenes of everyday life with extraordinary dynamism. Key Highlights of His Career The "Domenica del Corriere" Era: Starting in 1941, Molino became the primary cover artist for the magazine, succeeding Achille Beltrame. His work was characterized by a vibrant, "cinematic" style that made news stories feel urgent and intensely human. Artistic Style: His technique blended classical draftsmanship with a modern sense of movement. He was a master of gouache and tempera, known for his ability to render complex crowd scenes, facial expressions, and atmospheric lighting. Comic Books and Satire: Beyond news illustration, Molino was a prolific comic artist, contributing to titles like Topolino (Mickey Mouse) in Italy and creating the character Virus, il mago della foresta dead . He also excelled in caricature and fashion illustration. Cultural Legacy: In recent years, Molino gained posthumous viral fame for a 1962 illustration of a futuristic vehicle (the "Singoletta"), which many internet users jokingly interpreted as a prophecy of social distancing.
